annotations.description: DSV3 Worrier has Spirebluff Canal in hand but chose to cast Quantum Riddler for full cost (5 mana) before playing the land. They control 6 lands already (Steam Vents, Multiversal Passage, Riverpyre Verge, Steam Vents, Island + one more), but playing Spirebluff Canal first would give them an additional mana, potentially leaving mana open after casting the Riddler. More importantly, casting a 5-mana creature into an opponent who has 5 lands (including untapped sources) and has already shown countermagic (Three Steps Ahead in graveyard/exile) is risky. The Warp cost of {1}{U} would let them deploy the Riddler at instant speed (likely on opponent's end step) for only 2 mana, dodging sorcery-speed removal and leaving mana open for their own interaction (Into the Flood Maw, Torch the Tower). Casting at full cost taps out most of their mana and walks into potential countermagic or removal, while the Warp option was clearly superior here.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Quantum Riddler for full cost {3}{U}{U}, tapping most lands and deploying at sorcery speed.
annotations.betterLine: Play Spirebluff Canal first, then cast Quantum Riddler using Warp {1}{U} at instant speed (on opponent's end step), keeping mana open for interaction like Into the Flood Maw or Torch the Tower.

annotations.description: Duelist of the Mind's power equals cards drawn this turn, so it's currently attacking as a 0/3 (0 damage). Casting Winternight Stories precombat would draw 3 cards, making Duelist a 3/3 flyer and triggering Otter's prowess for +1/+1, adding ~4 damage to the attack. With 5 lands available, casting Winternight Stories for 3 mana still leaves 2 mana open for Torch the Tower or Into the Flood Maw as interaction. The opponent has no creatures on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting any spells precombat, attacking with Duelist of the Mind as a 0-power creature.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Winternight Stories precombat to draw 3 cards, making Duelist of the Mind a 3/3 flyer with vigilance and triggering Otter prowess, then attack for significantly more damage while still holding up 2 mana for interaction.

annotations.description: Spending 3 mana + 1 life during combat to create a Fish token is questionable when o3 Valley has Day of Judgment and Elspeth in hand as their primary game plan, and importantly holds No More Lies, Spell Snare, and Consult the Star Charts as reactive spells. The Fish token doesn't meaningfully impact the board against DSV3 Worrier's Duelist of the Mind and Otter Token, and using 4 mana (3 + tap Fountainport) during their own combat phase means they can't hold up No More Lies + Spell Snare simultaneously on the opponent's turn. They have 5 lands but Fountainport is now tapped, leaving only 4 mana sources available. With Sunken Citadel producing WW for abilities, they can still cast No More Lies (WU), but the mana is tighter than it needs to be. Keeping mana open for counterspells against an aggressive Izzet tempo deck with Stormchaser's Talent is generally more important than a 1/1 Fish.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Fountainport to create a 1/1 Fish token for 3 mana and 1 life during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Hold up all mana for the opponent's turn to maximize flexibility with No More Lies and Spell Snare, or wait until the opponent's end step to create the Fish if the mana isn't needed for counters.

annotations.description: Riverpyre Verge is arguably the weakest Demolition Field target. The opponent has multiple Islands/Mountains to enable it, and replacing it with a basic land barely changes their mana. A Steam Vents (typed Island Mountain, providing both colors untapped) or Spirebluff Canal would be slightly more disruptive to the opponent's color base.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Riverpyre Verge with Demolition Field
annotations.betterLine: Target a Steam Vents or Spirebluff Canal instead, as these true dual lands are harder to replace with a single basic land. The difference is small but Riverpyre Verge is the least impactful target.

annotations.description: o3 Valley is at 5 life facing a Duelist of the Mind (flying, vigilance) and Quantum Riddler (4/6 flying) on the opponent's board, with Fear of Missing Out on the stack (which enables extra combat phases with delirium). Fear of Missing Out costs 2 mana (mana value 2), and o3 Valley has Spell Snare in hand which counters spells with mana value 2 — a perfect answer. Alternatively, No More Lies could counter it. By letting Fear of Missing Out resolve, the opponent gets an extra combat phase trigger (with delirium likely active given graveyard contents), which combined with the existing flying threats at 5 life is extremely dangerous. The opponent attacks with 2 creatures after this resolves, likely dealing lethal or near-lethal damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to respond to Fear of Missing Out on the stack (chose -1, passing priority).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Spell Snare targeting Fear of Missing Out (mana value 2) to counter it, preventing the extra combat phase and the additional threat on board. This preserves life total and buys time to cast Day of Judgment next turn.
